## Dry-carry of passive tracers, and the zero-base guard {#sec-ch08-drycarry}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5 (chengcli/snapy)
sources: OUTLINE.md 8.13
status: draft
-->

### Summary

This is the one entry in the chapter that is not about positivity at all, and the distinction is worth
making loudly because its name and its neighbours both suggest otherwise. It keeps an arithmetic
expression finite. The tracer it protects can still go negative, and the repository's own test for it
accepts a negative value.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- When a forcing changes dry mass, the passive tracers must be carried with it.
- An addition carries the ratio at source entry; a removal carries the source-free stage ratio.
- A zero source-free density would make that ratio $0/0$, so it falls back to the entry ratio.
- This is a finiteness guard, not a positivity one: the result may legitimately be negative.
:::

### Derivation

A forcing that writes a dry-mass tendency has to say what happens to the tracers riding on that mass.
Addition and removal are not symmetric, and the code comment at
`carry_dry_source` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}) gives the reason: an addition carries the ratio as it stands at
source entry, while a removal carries the ratio the stage would have had with no source at all, so that
the removal cannot amplify a ratio that transport or the implicit solve has just changed.

Computing that source-free ratio means dividing the source-free scalar by the source-free density, and
nothing prevents that density from being zero in a cell that is empty with the source removed. The guard
at `rho_base` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}) substitutes the entry ratio there, which keeps the expression
finite.

What the guard does *not* do is bound the result. The repository's own test asserts a finite answer at a
zero base and accepts a bottom value of $-5\times10^{-4}$: a negative tracer is the expected outcome,
not a failure. Passive scalars under a dry sink have no positivity guarantee from this path or from any
other.

`[C9]` separates the three statements. Over $2\times10^5$ cells the stage moves the ratio away from its
entry value by up to $1.46$, so the two rules are genuinely different: carrying the source-free ratio
rather than the entry one changes the result by up to $1.16$ of scalar, and it is the entry rule that would
amplify the ratio transport has just changed. At a zero source-free density the guard returns the entry
ratio and the expression stays finite. It stays unbounded below all the same: under a dry sink $66\,587$ of
the $2\times10^5$ cells end with a negative scalar, worst $-1.4$
[check `src/snapy_report/ch08/positivity_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch08/positivity_check.out`].

### Numerical method

The carry is the lambda at `scalar_r` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}). The source-free density and scalar are
rebuilt by running the integrator's own stage combination on the tendency with the dry source subtracted
at `rho_base` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}), so the "source-free" state is the one the integrator would have
produced and not a cell-wise approximation of it. The choice between the two ratios is made per cell on
the sign of the dry source at `carry_r` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_dry_carry_zero_base.py` (`test_dry_carry_zero_base_python`) | a finite result at a zero base; the bottom scalar equals $-5\times10^{-4}$ | `1e-12` | `atol=1e-12`, `rtol=0` inline in `main` ({{< code tests/test_dry_carry_zero_base.py main >}}); the file gives no reason |
| `tests/test_stage_forcing_dry_tracer.py` (`test_stage_forcing_dry_tracer_python`) | a user stage forcing that writes dry mass carries its tracers | absolute $10^{-12}$ | set inline in `main`, on the tracer-ratio bounds and on the dry increment ({{< code tests/test_stage_forcing_dry_tracer.py main >}}); the file gives no reason |

: Tests of the dry-carry guard. {#tbl-ch08-drycarry-tests}

The first test is the clearest statement in the repository that this is not a positivity mechanism: it
asserts a negative value to twelve digits.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- No positivity guarantee for passive scalars under a dry sink. The guard keeps the arithmetic finite
  and nothing more.
:::

1. **A fallback, not a correction.** When the source-free density is zero the entry ratio is used
   instead. Whether that ratio is the physically right one in an emptied cell is not argued anywhere;
   it is the finite choice.
